text:
Ryan Hartman has been in two kinds of headlines this month. One kind was his two goals in Boston on Nov. 14 during Minnesota's winning streak. The other was a report from Heavy.com that the Wild's latest offer to Detroit for Dylan Larkin includes him. Nothing has happened, but it is hard to ignore when you are a veteran depth forward on a team that wants a top center.

His season sits in between. He has 3 goals and 4 assists in 24 games playing 13.2 minutes a night, mostly in a bottom-six role. The results with him on the ice have been rough: Minnesota gets only 40% of the expected goals at five-on-five when he plays, the share of chance quality, and 15.8 points worse than when he sits.

That is a long way from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him driving play in the 89th percentile among forwards and drawing more penalties than he took. Our talent range still sees him as a 1.6 to 2.3 points-per-60 player. Watch whether the shooting comes back up from 10%, and whether he is still in Minnesota by the deadline.
headline: A name in the Larkin talks
